title: Distinct components of a Noetherian curve meet in finitely many closed points
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] with topological Krull dimension $\dim Y\le 1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] form a finite family. For two distinct components $Z_i,Z_j$, every point of $Z_i\cap Z_j$ is closed in $Y$ and the intersection is finite. Consequently the union $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}(Z_i\cap Z_j)$ is a finite set of closed points; if $y\notin T$, it lies on exactly one component.
